text:
sam: quick UX q in the Dedicated Pool form — do we go inline errors only or keep a top error summary for the submit flow? i prototyped both.
maria: inline for this specific form. six fields, users fix one thing and move on. top summary is better for 20+ field forms.
cheng: inline also aligns with our formik validators. can auto-focus first invalid field on submit.
jess: counter: when multiple errors exist (min > max, missing billing tag, invalid name) seeing them at a glance is helpful. propose inline + a small persistent banner after submit: "3 errors — see fields".
kevin: a11y: if inline-only, add an aria-live region that announces "3 errors" and move focus to the first invalid control. screen reader users need that summary.
sam: what about required markers? asterisk only vs explicit "Required" label. product asked for explicit for audit reasons.
maria: explicit is clearer but heavy. suggestion: asterisk on desktop, explicit tiny "Required" underneath label on mobile. keeps desktop tidy.
cheng: dev note: reserving space under labels prevents layout shifts if we show/hide the word. avoids content jumps.
jess: also: destructive copy on pool page. current: "Delete pool" + typed-confirm with "delete pool". suggest more explicit: "Delete pool and all cached artifacts — irreversible". require full pool name and a "I understand charges may persist" checkbox.
kevin: modal must be role=alertdialog, focus trapped, confirmation input with aria-label that details consequences, and keyboard accessible.
maria: CTA language: primary should read "Delete pool" and be critical color; secondary "Cancel". add a small "Export logs" link in modal to reduce accidental data loss.
sam: decision proposal: inline field errors + persistent top banner on submit with "View all errors" anchor that opens a compact in-page list and jumps to first error. asterisk on desktop, explicit "Required" on mobile. destructive modal: explicit copy, typed-confirm full name + checkbox, role=alertdialog.
cheng: i'll prototype the aria-live and the banner behaviour (jump + in-page list). question: should the banner also include keyboard focusable links to each error?
jess: yes — keyboard focusable anchors that move to each invalid field are ideal. minimal list (ul) so screen readers get structure.
sam: i'll update figma and submit a tiny PR touching formik onSubmit. will tag you all for review.
kevin: i'll add an a11y checklist in the PR.
design-bot: fig link uploaded: https://figma.redwood/app/file/PoolFormV3 — comments enabled.
sam: thanks, will post PR link when ready :thumbsup:
